answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A timber delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A dune check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A horizon penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 868 identities need 868 bonds of 78 tokens, 38542 dollars of hardware and 11 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
